justifications.functional_suitability: Catalog Service (Search Index Manager), Order & Checkout Service, Review Service and Recommendation Service cover R-01 to R-04. Gaps: no cart component, no ratings aggregation, no ebook delivery, no multi-currency or admin elements, no identity service; Review Service components are thin.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Distributed Caching Container (ElastiCache, Redlock stampede protection), Cache-Aside in Catalog Service, CQRS Search Index Manager, SQS/SNS decoupling, CDN, and Recommendation <200ms fallback. Gaps: no explicit autoscaling, no concrete 3G page-load or 1M MAU capacity mechanisms.
justifications.compatibility: Defined integrations with Payment Gateway, Shipping Providers, Tax Calculation Service via REST/gRPC/HTTPS and OpenAPI at API Gateway. Gaps: no anti-corruption layer for varied shipping APIs, multi-currency only mentioned, inconsistent protocols (SQS/SNS to external payment).
justifications.usability: SPA / Mobile Client with User Interface View and offline State Management serves customers; the Store Administrator is routed through the same client with no dedicated admin interface or catalog management component. No localization or accessibility mechanisms.
justifications.reliability: Circuit Breaker and Load Balancer, Bulkhead Thread Pools, Message Outbox, Idempotency Ledger, Saga orchestrators, health probes, multi-region replication and Event Archive. Gaps: no explicit failover/backup/RTO design for 99.95%, probes absent in some services.
justifications.security: CDN and WAF, Authentication and Security Filter (OAuth2/JWT), TLS 1.3, Secrets Manager, KMS Cryptographic Erasure Engine, SIEM Provider, immutable Compliance/Archival Store, input sanitization. Gaps: no explicit OWASP mapping, RBAC for administrators, or service-to-service authentication.
justifications.maintainability: Independent microservices with database-per-service, layered Order & Checkout components, Message Broker decoupling, Flyway migrations, OpenTelemetry, and signed CI/CD Configuration Bundler. Gaps: technology choices left open (Java or Node.js), shared Compliance/User Data Container blurs isolation, and some component models are inconsistent.
justifications.portability: Multi-region AWS design (ElastiCache Global Datasets, Aurora replication) fits target regions; SPA and mobile clients are portable. Heavy AWS-specific services (SQS/SNS, KMS, Secrets Manager) with no abstraction layers or containerization/IaC details limit replaceability.

sensitivity_points: No explicit autoscaling or compute platform defined
tradeoffs: Caching speeds reads but risks stale catalog data
PERF-01.justification: CDN, ElastiCache cache-aside, and CQRS search index support fast reads. But autoscaling, compute platform, and 3G payload optimization are unspecified, so the 10x load measure is unproven.

sensitivity_points: Recompute workload shares Compliance/User Data Container database
tradeoffs: Async training decouples browsing but recommendations become stale
PERF-02.justification: Event-driven training is decoupled from the request path via the broker. The service has its own database, cache fallbacks, and a 200ms timeout. Batch recompute resource isolation is not explicit.

sensitivity_points: Shipping calls must be truly asynchronous with retries
tradeoffs: Deferred shipping gives resilience but delays fulfillment confirmation
AVAIL-01.justification: Saga orchestration, outbox, SQS/SNS to shipping, and idempotency support deferring shipping. The model does not show retry or DLQ for shipping, and the order flow is ambiguous.

sensitivity_points: Database replication lag affects lost orders
tradeoffs: Multi-region replication improves availability but adds cost and consistency complexity
AVAIL-02.justification: Multi-region Aurora and ElastiCache global datasets are mentioned, with edge multi-region routing. No explicit failover, RPO/RTO, or health-based routing, so no-lost-orders and 99.95% are unproven.

sensitivity_points: No dedicated pricing or currency component
tradeoffs: Delegating to payment gateway simplifies integration but hides currency logic
MOD-01.justification: No pricing or currency component or configuration mechanism exists. Currency logic would be spread across Catalog, Order, and the gateway adapter, so changes likely exceed the pricing and payment scope.

sensitivity_points: Shared database container and event schema coupling
tradeoffs: Service isolation eases replacement but constrains shared data models
MOD-02.justification: Recommendation is a separate microservice with an inference engine encapsulated behind an API controller. The algorithm can change locally if API and event contracts are stable, though it shares the data container.

sensitivity_points: Sanitization present only in Review Service; Catalog lacks explicit parameterization
tradeoffs: Edge filtering adds latency but blocks attacks early
SEC-01.justification: WAF, gateway request validation, review input sanitization, OpenAPI validation, and SIEM logging give layered defenses. Search lacks explicit injection protection like parameterized queries, and output encoding is not shown.

sensitivity_points: No orchestrated deletion across all services
Immutable archives and event archive conflict with deletion
tradeoffs: Immutable audit retention conflicts with right to erasure
SEC-02.justification: Crypto erasure and an anonymization worker exist, but only Review is wired. There is no deletion request flow across services, nor verification, and event and archive stores may retain personal data.
